title: Key vowel sounds
goal: Hear and say the French u and ou, é and è, and the three nasal vowels, so that tu and tout, vin and vent stop sounding the same.

items.note: The ou sound, like English “too”. The t is silent.
The French u sound. Don't say “roo”: that is roue (wheel).
Both vowels are the an/en nasal sound. Un enfant (boy), une enfant (girl).
bon has a nasal vowel; in bonne you hear the n.

items.fr: u / ou · é / è · an, on, in
items.en: key French vowel sounds and their spellings

drills.prompt: Which word has the French u sound (say “ee”, then round your lips)?
drills.explain: The letter u alone makes the rounded “ee” sound. The spelling ou sounds like English “oo”.

drills.prompt: In which word is the n NOT pronounced?
drills.explain: In bon, on is a nasal vowel. When a vowel follows (bonne, une), you hear the n.

blocks.body: Listen again and hunt for the sounds of this lesson: **ou** in [[vous]], [[pour]], [[tout]]; **u** in [[du]]; **é** in [[désirez]], [[café]], [[thé]]; **è** in [[très]]; nasal vowels in [[bonjour]], [[un]], [[pain]].

blocks.title: 1. u and ou
blocks.body:
- **ou** sounds like the *oo* in English “too”: [[vous]], [[tout]], [[bonjour]].
- **u** has no English equivalent. Say “ee”, keep your tongue exactly there, and **round your lips** as if to whistle. That is [[tu]], [[rue]], [[salut]].

This difference changes the meaning, so it is worth the effort: [[tu]] means *you*, [[tout]] means *all*.

blocks.title: u or ou? Minimal pairs
head: u
meaning
ou
meaning
blocks.note: Tap the speaker: you hear the u word, then the ou word.

blocks.title: 2. é and è
blocks.body:
- **é** is a tight, smiling sound, like “ay” in *say* but shorter, with no glide at the end: [[café]], [[thé]] (tea), [[et]] (and). The ending **-er** often sounds the same, as in [[parler]] (to speak).
- **è** is more open, like the *e* in *bet*: [[très]], [[mère]], [[père]]. The letters **ê** ([[fête]], party) and often **ai** ([[s'il vous plaît]]) make this sound too.

A clear pair is [[les]] (the, plural) / [[lait]] (milk). You may also see [[et]] (and) / [[est]] (is): many speakers say et with é and est with è, but many others say them the same way. Speakers often blend é and è in some words, so don't worry too much; just make **é** clear and tight.

blocks.title: 3. The nasal vowels
blocks.body:
A **nasal vowel** is a vowel said with air going through your nose. When a vowel is followed by **n** or **m** at the end of a word (or before another consonant), the n is **not pronounced**: it just makes the vowel nasal.

- **an / en / am / em**: an open “ah” through the nose: [[enfant]] (child), [[France]], [[maman]] (mom).
- **on / om**: an “oh” through the nose: [[bonjour]], [[non]], [[nom]].
- **in / ain / un**: a flat “a” (as in *cat*) through the nose: [[vin]] (wine), [[pain]] (bread), [[bien]] (well), [[un]] (one, a). Many speakers in France say [[un]] exactly like [[in]]; in Québec, [[un]] usually keeps its own, rounder sound (see the Canada note).

If a vowel comes right after the n, or the n is doubled, the vowel is **not** nasal and you hear the n: [[bon]] → [[bonne]], [[un]] → [[une]].

blocks.title: Three nasal vowels side by side
blocks.note: Say each set slowly. Only the vowel changes; there is never an n sound at the end.

examples.en: good (m), good (f): the n appears in bonne
a (m), a (f): the n appears in une

blocks.title: Mouth tricks
blocks.body:
- **French u:** whistle position. Say “eeee”, then slowly push your lips forward into a small circle without moving your tongue. If it starts to sound like “oo”, your tongue moved back.
- **é:** smile slightly and keep your jaw still. English speakers add a little “y” at the end (“kaf-ay-ee”); stop the sound cleanly: [[café]].
- **Nasals:** hold your nose gently and say [[bon]]. You should feel a buzz. Now say it again **without** touching the tongue to the roof of your mouth: that is the trick to avoid an English n.
- **oui** is one quick syllable: “wee”.

- **Saying “oo” for u:** [[tu]] becomes [[tout]] and [[vu]] becomes [[vous]]. Keep the tongue forward for u.
- **Adding an n:** [[bon]] is not “bone” or “bon-n”. Don't touch your tongue to your teeth.
- **Mixing un and une:** [[un]] has a nasal vowel, [[une]] has the u sound plus a clear n. This tells the listener if a word is masculine or feminine.
- **Pronouncing every letter:** in [[pain]], [[vin]], [[tout]], the final letters are silent. (More in lesson 4.)

Québec French has a few vowel habits that surprise newcomers:

- Before **i** and **u**, the letters **t** and **d** often sound like *ts* and *dz*: [[tu]] sounds like “tsu”, [[du]] like “dzu”, [[lundi]] (Monday) like “lun-dzi”. This is normal and correct in Québec.
- In Québec, [[un]] and [[in]] usually still sound different. In much of France, many people pronounce them the same way.
- Some vowels are longer, and can “glide” a little, in words like [[père]] or [[fête]].

You don't need to copy these features, but knowing them will help you understand people around you.

blocks.prompt: In which word do you hear an n sound?
blocks.explain: The n is heard only when a vowel follows it: une. In un, bon and vin, the n just makes the vowel nasal.

blocks.prompt: Match the French and the English.

[[père]] and [[mère]] have è (open sound); [[et]] has the tight é sound.
non: nasal on, no n sound at the end.
You hear the n: [[bonne]]. In [[bon]], the n is silent.

blocks.prompt: You are at a café. Greet the server and order a coffee and some bread, politely. When asked « C'est tout ? », say yes, that's all, and thank them. Focus on clear u, ou, é and nasal vowels.

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Bonjour ! Un café et du pain, s'il vous plaît. … Oui, c'est tout. Merci beaucoup !
models.en: Hello! A coffee and some bread, please. … Yes, that's all. Thank you very much!

blocks.prompt: Make your own sound map: write two words from this unit for each sound: u, ou, é, è, an/en, on, in/un.

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: u : tu, rue. ou : vous, bonjour. é : café, et. è : très, mère. an/en : enfant, vent. on : bon, non. in/un : vin, pain.
models.en: u: you, street. ou: you (formal), hello. é: coffee, and. è: very, mother. an/en: child, wind. on: good, no. in/un: wine, bread.

summary:
- Tell **u** ([[tu, rue]]) from **ou** ([[tout, vous]])
- Make a tight **é** ([[café]]) and an open **è** ([[très, mère]])
- Say the three nasal vowels without an n: [[vent, vont, vin]]
- Hear when the n comes back: [[bon / bonne]], [[un / une]]
